StrokeProfileStop

A stop of the stroke profile of a path, see path.strokeProfile: the pen that draws its stroke at an offset along the path, an ellipse with a width, an aspect and an angle. Between the stops, each of them changes along the path, easing into and out of smooth stops and in straight lines from the others, see smooth. A stop can set only some of them, and leave the others to the stops around it.

Constructors

StrokeProfileStop([object])

Creates a stroke profile stop.

    Parameters:

  • object: Object — the properties of the stop, its offset, width, aspect, angle and smooth — optional

    Returns:

  • StrokeProfileStop

Example:

var path = new Path.Line([20, 50], [180, 50]);
path.strokeColor = 'black';
path.strokeWidth = 10;
path.strokeProfile = [
    new StrokeProfileStop({ offset: 0, width: 0.5 }),
    new StrokeProfileStop({ offset: 160, width: 2 })
];

Properties

path

The path whose stroke profile the stop is part of.

Read only.

    Type:

  • Path⟋null
offset

The offset of the stop along its path, as in path.getPointAt(offset). Unlike the offset of gradient stops, it is a length, not a fraction. The stop stays between the same segments when they move, so its offset changes with the lengths of the curves before it.

    Type:

  • Number
width

The width of the pen at the stop, as a factor of the path’s style.strokeWidth: 1 for the stroke width, 2 for twice as wide. Stops without a width leave it to the stops around them, and without any, it is 1.

    Type:

  • Number⟋null
aspect

The aspect of the pen at the stop: its height as a factor of its width, 1 for a round pen, less for a flat nib. Stops without an aspect leave it to the stops around them, and without any, it is 1.

    Type:

  • Number⟋null
angle

The angle of the pen at the stop, in degrees, in the path’s coordinates. Angles aren’t wrapped: from 0 at one stop to 720 at the next, the pen turns twice. Stops without an angle leave it to the stops around them, and without any, it is 0.

    Type:

  • Number⟋null
smooth

Whether the values ease into and out of the stop: they arrive at it and leave it flat, and between two smooth stops, a value follows a cubic from one to the other, without overshooting them. As the slopes don’t depend on other stops, changing a stop only changes the values up to the stops on either side of it. Without smoothing, the values change in straight lines to the stops on either side.

    Default:

  • true

    Type:

  • Boolean

Methods

clone()

    Returns:

  • StrokeProfileStop — a copy of the stop, without a path
equals(stop)

Checks whether the stop is equal to the supplied one.

    Parameters:

  • stop: StrokeProfileStop

    Returns:

  • Boolean — true if they are equal, false otherwise
